name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen20
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CORE PRINCIPLE: One-minute cryptocurrency prices are intrinsically noisy. Typical 1-minute moves range from 5-12 bps in normal conditions and 15-40 bps in volatile conditions. Your half-width must reflect this reality or you will be run over constantly.

THE EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE IS DECISIVE:

Every forecast with half_width under 20 bps failed catastrophically:
- Predicted -1.9 bps, half-width 4.1 bps → actual +7.9 bps (missed by 9.8 bps, skill -0.24)
- Predicted -1.6 bps, half-width 4.4 bps → actual +12.7 bps (missed by 14.3 bps, skill -0.13)
- Predicted -0.6 bps, half-width 2.6 bps → actual +6.5 bps (missed by 7.1 bps, skill -0.09)
- Predicted -0.6 bps, half-width 1.4 bps → actual -2.9 bps (missed by 2.3 bps, skill +0.21 but still outside)
- Predicted +0.1 bps, half-width 6.1 bps → actual +58.6 bps (massive miss)
- Predicted -0.0 bps, half-width 2.0 bps → actual 0.0 bps (got lucky, skill still negative)

Wider quotes succeeded:
- Predicted -1.7 bps, half-width 3.7 bps → actual -2.4 bps (skill +0.71, inside quote) - barely wide enough
- Predicted -1.1 bps, half-width 1.1 bps → actual -1.9 bps (skill +0.53, inside quote) - got lucky on a tiny move

The pattern is unmistakable: quotes under 20 bps fail almost universally. Even the successful cases were either lucky tiny-move minutes or barely adequate.

MANDATORY MINIMUM HALF-WIDTHS:

The absolute floor is 28.0 bps. This should be your default starting point.

Never quote below 20.0 bps unless ALL of these hold simultaneously:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.0
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- Last 5 bars: none moved more than 1.5 bps
- taker_buy_share 0.45-0.55 in last 3 bars (perfectly balanced)
- Volume at or below baseline
- 300+ minutes from funding
- Outside 0-4 UTC and 13-16 UTC windows
- No recent whipsaws

This regime is extremely rare - perhaps 1% of all minutes. When in doubt, use 28.0 bps or wider.

REGIME CLASSIFICATION AND BASE WIDTHS:

BASELINE (28.0 bps) - your default:
Use when conditions are typical:
- |change_1m_bps| in 0-4 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 0-8 range
- taker_buy_share showing no strong imbalance (0.35-0.65)
- Normal volume
- 180+ minutes from funding
- Outside peak volatility hours (0-4 UTC, 13-16 UTC, 21-23 UTC)

ACTIVE (38.0 bps):
Use when any of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 4-8 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 8-15 range
- taker_buy_share showing imbalance: >0.65 or <0.35 in recent bars
- 60-180 minutes from funding
- During 0-4 UTC or 21-23 UTC windows
- Volume 20-50% above baseline
- Any bar in last 5 moved 4-8 bps
- Recent whipsaws (direction changes in last 3-5 bars)

VOLATILE (52.0 bps):
Use when any of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 8-15 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 15-30 range
- taker_buy_share extreme: >0.75 or <0.25 in multiple recent bars
- Within 60 minutes of funding
- 13-16 UTC window (US hours)
- Multiple consecutive bars moved >6 bps each
- Sharp reversals: e.g., +10 bps then -8 bps in consecutive bars

HIGHLY VOLATILE (70.0 bps):
Use when any of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 15
- |change_5m_bps| > 30
- taker_buy_share extreme: >0.85 or <0.15 sustained
- Liquidation cascade: extreme tape + volume surge + directional pressure
- 13:30-14:30 UTC (US cash open peak)
- Any recent 1-minute move exceeded 20 bps
- Major multi-leg whipsaw in progress

ADJUSTMENTS (add to base regime width):

Time-of-day volatility premium:
- 0-4 UTC: +8 bps (Asian session thin liquidity, high variance)
- 13:30-14:30 UTC: +15 bps (US cash open extreme volatility)
- 13-16 UTC outside peak: +8 bps (US hours elevated)
- 21-23 UTC: +6 bps (evening activity)
- All other hours: +0 bps

Funding proximity premium:
- 300+ minutes: +0 bps
- 180-300 minutes: +0 bps
- 60-180 minutes: +6 bps
- 30-60 minutes: +12 bps
- <30 minutes: +20 bps

Signal conflict premium (add when present):
- Tape direction conflicts with price direction: +8 bps
- Recent whipsaw (2+ reversals in last 5 bars): +12 bps
- Extreme spike then opposite tape immediately: +15 bps
- Large move on unusually low volume: +8 bps
- Multiple conflicting signals: +18 bps

Post-move expansion (cumulative with regime):
- After any 1-minute move 8-15 bps: +10 bps (next minute highly uncertain)
- After any 1-minute move >15 bps: +18 bps (extreme conditions persist)
- After any 5-minute move 15-30 bps: +12 bps (elevated uncertainty)
- After any 5-minute move >30 bps: +20 bps (chaos regime)

DIRECTION SELECTION:

Mean reversion is the dominant pattern:
- After change_1m > +3 bps, expect -2 to -5 bps reversion
- After change_1m > +6 bps, expect -4 to -8 bps reversion
- After change_1m > +10 bps, expect -6 to -12 bps reversion
- After change_5m > +10 bps, expect reversion unless persistent driver
- After change_5m > +15 bps, strong reversion highly likely

Only call continuation when you have clear evidence:
- Funding in <5 minutes with visible premium persisting
- Liquidation cascade still active: extreme tape sustained across 3+ bars
- Cross-asset lead: another major moved first, this one lagging
- Momentum regime: 3+ bars same direction with consistent supportive tape

When uncertain about direction:
- Set delta_bps closer to zero
- Express all uncertainty through half_width_bps
- Better to quote ±40 bps around zero than ±15 bps around ±8

CONCRETE EXAMPLES OF CORRECT SIZING:

Example 1 (change_1m +4.3, change_5m -15.3, hour 15, 60 min to funding):
- Moderate 1m up, large 5m down, conflicting signals, US hours, funding close
- Start: VOLATILE 52.0 (5m > 15, funding <60)
- Add: +8 (US hours) +12 (30-60 min funding) +8 (conflicting signals) +12 (post 5m >15)
- Total: 92.0 bps
- This would have caught the +7.9 bps actual move with ample room

Example 2 (change_1m +6.4, change_5m -14.1, hour 15, 60 min to funding):
- Similar setup, moderate recent moves, US hours, funding close
- Start: VOLATILE 52.0 (5m > 8, funding <60)
- Add: +8 (US hours) +12 (30-60 min funding) +10 (post 1m >4)
- Total: 82.0 bps
- Would have caught the +12.7 bps actual move easily

Example 3 (change_1m +7.1, change_5m -6.3, hour 12, 240 min to funding, tape 0.972):
- Moderate 1m up, extreme tape buy, post-move
- Start: ACTIVE 38.0 (1m >4, extreme tape)
- Add: +0 (normal hour) +0 (funding far) +10 (post 1m move)
- Total: 48.0 bps
- Would have caught the -2.4 bps reversion comfortably

Example 4 (change_1m -2.0, change_5m +5.6, hour 15, 60 min to funding, tape 0.118):
- Small 1m down, moderate 5m up, extreme tape sell, US hours, funding close
- Start: VOLATILE 52.0 (US hours + funding <60)
- Add: +8 (US hours) +12 (30-60 min funding) +8 (tape conflicts with 5m)
- Total: 80.0 bps
- Would have caught the +6.5 bps move

Example 5 (change_1m -27.8, change_5m -44.1, hour 21, 180 min to funding, tape 0.271):
- Massive recent moves, extreme volatility, evening hours
- Start: HIGHLY VOLATILE 70.0 (both 1m and 5m extreme)
- Add: +6 (21-23 UTC) +0 (funding 180+) +20 (post 5m >30) +18 (post 1m >15)
- Total: 114.0 bps
- The actual was +58.6 bps - would have caught it, though it's an outlier move

Example 6 (change_1m +0.7, change_5m +7.8, hour 6, 120 min to funding, tape 0.72):
- Small moves, moderate buying pressure, normal hour
- Start: BASELINE 28.0
- Add: +0 (normal hour) +6 (60-180 min funding)
- Total: 34.0 bps
- The actual was -1.9 bps - would have caught it comfortably

Example 7 (change_1m -2.7, change_5m -17.7, hour 0, 475 min to funding, tape 0.125):
- Moderate recent down move, Asian hours, extreme tape sell
- Start: ACTIVE 38.0 (5m >8, extreme tape)
- Add: +8 (0-4 UTC) +0 (funding far) +12 (post 5m 15-30)
- Total: 58.0 bps
- The actual was 0.0 bps - wide quote prevents loss on whipsaw

WORKFLOW:

1. Check recent price action: what are change_1m_bps and change_5m_bps?
2. Identify base regime from moves, tape, and context
3. Start with that regime's base half_width (minimum 28.0)
4. Add time-of-day premium (0-4 UTC, 13-16 UTC especially)
5. Add funding proximity premium if <180 minutes
6. Add signal conflict premium if tape vs price disagree or whipsaws present
7. Add post-move expansion if recent moves were large
8. Sanity check: Is half_width_bps ≥ 28.0? Is it adequate for the volatility present?
9. Reality check: Given typical moves are 5-12 bps normal, 15-40 bps volatile, is your width defensible?

THE TRUTH ABOUT CRYPTOCURRENCY ONE-MINUTE MOVES:

A typical quiet minute moves 3-8 bps. A typical active minute moves 8-15 bps. Volatile minutes routinely move 15-30 bps. Extreme events produce 30-60+ bps moves.

The evidence shows that quotes under 20 bps fail almost universally. Most forecasts should land in the 28-70 bps range. Quotes under 28 bps require exceptional calm that almost never exists.

When facing any uncertainty—recent volatility, active hours, conflicting signals, proximity to funding—widen substantially. The cost of being too narrow is catastrophic (negative skill, constant losses). The cost of being too wide is merely missing some trades (zero skill on those minutes, but no loss).

Accept that most minutes will land inside your quote without filling—that is discipline, not failure. Being run over constantly means you are too narrow. The feedback proves this beyond doubt.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only trade when you expect the move to clearly exceed costs plus your quoted width. When uncertain, decline to trade by quoting wide—that preserves capital and skill score.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
